rich_summary: Priests advise King Janamejaya to perform a divinely ordained "snake‑sacrifice" described in the Puranas to destroy Takshaka, the serpent responsible for his father’s death. The king orders preparations, and a vast sacrificial platform is built according to Vedic rules. During construction, a learned builder ominously predicts that the ritual will ultimately be halted by a Brahmana, prompting the king to restrict entry to the ceremony. When the sacrifice begins, priests clad in black pour ghee into the sacred fire while chanting the names of serpents, magically drawing snakes from across the world into the flames. Multitudes—of every size and color—fall screaming into the fire, filling the air with smoke, stench, and terror. As the slaughter unfolds, Takshaka flees to Indra’s palace seeking divine protection, setting up the coming intervention that may stop the catastrophic ritual.

highlight_spans.why: The priests introduce the divinely sanctioned snake‑sacrifice, establishing the central ritual that drives the episode.
The builder’s prophecy that a Brahmana will halt the sacrifice foreshadows the pivotal interruption that will later save the serpent race.
The formal commencement of the snake‑sacrifice marks the transition from preparation to the catastrophic ritual itself.
The vivid depiction of countless snakes falling helplessly into the fire conveys the horror and emotional intensity of the massacre.
Takshaka fleeing to Indra for protection shifts the narrative from ritual destruction to divine intervention and the coming turning point.

top_scenes.scene_text: Vedic priests in black garments chant beside a विशाल sacrificial altar as serpents of many colors are magically dragged through the air and tumble screaming into a towering column of fire.
Huge serpents—some horse‑sized, some thick as elephant trunks—twist together midair above the blazing yajna fire before plunging into the flames.
The serpent king Takshaka, terrified, coils before Indra in a radiant celestial palace, pleading for protection from the deadly sacrifice on earth.
